name: Commerce rule restricts chip exports to data centers serving D:5 firms
title: Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors
headline: Commerce rule restricts chip exports to data centers serving D:5 firms
lede: Overseas data centers become harder to supply with advanced US chips if they remotely provide significant compute to companies headquartered in Country Group D:5 or Macau.

effects.effect: Data centers must vet customer ownership before supplying compute
Training runs by D:5-headquartered firms on US chips get harder

appearances.title: Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors
appearances.headline: Commerce rule restricts chip exports to data centers serving D:5 firms
appearances.newly_constrained: Overseas data centers become harder to supply with advanced US chips if they remotely provide significant compute to companies headquartered in Country Group D:5 or Macau.
appearances.why: Cloud compute providers and their customers now face due diligence on ownership ties to D:5 countries or Macau.
appearances.limits: interim final rule; volume threshold for significant compute not stated in summary

ripples.effect: Data centers must vet customer ownership before supplying compute
Training runs by D:5-headquartered firms on US chips get harder

sources.name: Federal Register
sources.title: Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors

constraint.who: Overseas data centers, foreign foundries, chip exporters, and D:5 or Macau headquartered firms
constraint.quote: These restrictions will undermine the ability of companies headquartered in countries of concern from using U.S. advanced Super Intelligence (SI) semiconductors to train advanced SI models.
constraint.harder: Overseas data centers that remotely supply significant compute to companies headquartered in Country Group D:5 or Macau face new export restrictions, and chip exporters, foundries and data centers must perform due diligence on customers.
